meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (República de Panamá) - unitary national jurisdiction
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified system; with substantial Anglo-American commercial law influence in corporate, maritime and trust services)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force since 2012)
Panama-UK Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1982, in force 1992)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 32 de 1927 (Sociedades Anónimas); Ley No. 23 de 2015 (AML/CFT) as amended by Ley No. 70 de 2019 and Ley No. 89 de 2021; Decreto de Gabinete No. 258 de 2016 (Unidad de Análisis Financiero - UAF); Ley No. 52 de 2016 (bearer-share immobilization); Decreto Ejecutivo No. 496 de 2020 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales); GAFILAT/FATF Recommendations 24 and 25

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificado de Búsqueda y Reserva de Nombre - corporate name clearance certificate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Público de Panamá (Dirección de Registro Mercantil)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Panamá) when the certificate will be used in foreign filings; notarized copy accepted for domestic use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Due diligence identity package: certified passport copy, proof of residential address and curriculum of each shareholder and director (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign national passport authority and notary public of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the originating State, followed by sworn Spanish translation by a Panamanian public translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating bank (correspondent or wealth-management institution) or licensed attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (competent authority of the originating State) combined with notarized signature; consular legalization if originating from a non-Hague State

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Poder) granted by the shareholders to the Panamanian resident agent for pre-incorporation filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholders' jurisdiction (or Panamanian notary when executed in Panama)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the originating State and sworn Spanish translation; execution before a Panamanian notary eliminates the apostille requirement for domestic proceedings

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 32 de 1927, sobre Sociedades Anónimas (Panama General Corporation Law), as amended; applicable provisions on corporate formation, share capital, registered office, resident agent, directors, and officers (Arts. 1-20 and related corporate governance articles).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Mercantile Section (Registro Público de Panamá, Sección Mercantil)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation / Articles of Incorporation), inscribed in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required; the corporation must have at least one issued share. In practice the initial capital is commonly declared as US$10,000, subscribed and either paid or stated as unpaid. No escrow deposit or capital bank account is required by Panamanian law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Corporation hereby issues and accepts the subscription of 10,000 common shares, par value US$1.00 each, to the founding shareholders named in the share register. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office shall be [address in Panama City, Republic of Panama], and the law firm [firm name] is appointed resident agent. RESOLVED FURTHER that [full name] is elected President, [full name] Secretary, and [full name] Treasurer, each with authority to open bank accounts, sign commercial contracts, and execute statutory filings. RESOLVED FURTHER that the corporate seal, minute book, and share ledger are adopted and kept by the Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Mercantile Section, name service desk and online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name application for the proposed Sociedad Anónima, including the corporate purpose and two alternative names. Pay the name-search fee and obtain the non-opposition name certificate. The certificate is valid for a limited period and must accompany the public deed.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of the applicant
Power of attorney if an agent files
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or opposed, submit a written reconsideration or reapply with an alternative name. If the certificate expires, obtain a re-issuance before executing the public deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Escritura Pública de Constitución
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Panama (Notaría Pública) or licensed law firm with notarial facilities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the public deed of incorporation containing the corporate name, registered office, resident agent, capital structure, share classes, directors, officers, purpose, and term. The incorporators or their attorneys-in-fact appear before the notary, execute the deed, and the notary authenticates it for Registry filing.
required_dossiers: Passports or identity cards of initial shareholders and directors
Power of attorney if subscribers appoint representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, amend the draft and execute a corrective addendum or re-execute the deed before another notary. Missing consent documents must be supplied before protocolization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama – Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authenticated public deed and required copies with the Mercantile Section. Pay the official inscription fee. The Registry reviews legal compliance, assigns the corporate registration number, and issues the registered extract and certificate of legal existence (Certificado de Personería Jurídica).
required_dossiers: Original notarized Escritura Pública de Constitución
Proof of payment of official fees
Power of attorney for the filing attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a preventive note or objection, file a corrective written brief within the legal term, have the notary issue a clarification or amendment deed, and pay any fee deficiency. The corporation is legally constituted as of the date and time of inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution and Organizational Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office and resident agent of the corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first meeting of the board of directors or obtain unanimous written consent. Adopt the pro-forma First Board Resolution approving the share subscription, registered office, resident agent, and officers. Open the corporate minute book, stock and transfer ledger, accounting records, and adopt the corporate seal. Issue share certificates to the subscribing shareholders.
required_dossiers: Directors' written waiver or meeting notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any organizational act is defective, the board may adopt a subsequent ratifying resolution correcting the error and place it in the corporate minute book. No Registry filing is required for internal board resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RUC, Aviso de Operación and Municipal Patent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; municipality (Alcaldía) of the business location
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the registered corporate documents, file the taxpayer registration with DGI to obtain the RUC and the Aviso de Operación allowing commencement of commercial activities. Subsequently apply to the local municipality for the Patente Municipal and pay the annual municipal patent tax. For pure wholesale distribution of green coffee beans, no sector-specific manufacturing license is triggered.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the registered Escritura Pública
Lease contract or title deed for registered office and warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the municipality returns the application, correct the inconsistencies through the DGI Sede Electrónica or municipal window. Late filing may incur a surcharge but the Aviso de Operación can be obtained, re-issued, or amended before operational inspection becomes final.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAmbiente); Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL); local municipality
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the green coffee distribution warehouse becomes operational, complete the applicable low-impact environmental registration with MiAmbiente, obtain the fire-safety inspection certificate from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, and file the workplace health-and-safety acknowledgment with MITRADEL. These clearances are physical operational prerequisites, not corporate incorporation licenses.
required_dossiers: Aviso de Operación and Patente Municipal
Warehouse address, floor plan, and structural description
Fire protection and emergency egress report
Waste handling manifests or storage plan for damaged coffee beans
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an inspection fails, correct the cited fire, structural, or sanitary deficiencies and request a re-inspection. If MiAmbiente classifies the operation as higher risk, submit the additional technical dossier or full environmental impact assessment before operations proceed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industry-specific licensing board is triggered for pure wholesale distribution of green coffee beans under ISIC 4631. The Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) is the general trade and commerce authority; the local municipality administers the Patente Municipal.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (tax and commercial operation notice) and Patente Municipal (municipal operating patent).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAmbiente) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I / low-impact registration (Diagnóstico Ambiental) may be required for the warehouse and distribution activity; no full environmental impact assessment is required unless processing or as-yet-undetermined high-impact thresholds are triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No untreated process wastewater may be discharged; sanitary wastewater must comply with the applicable parameters of Decreto Ejecutivo No. 309 de 2000, including pH, BOD/COD, TSS, and oil and grease limits set by MiAmbiente. Coffee dust and other particulates from green coffee handling must remain below Panamanian ambient air quality standards. Coffee bean residues and damaged lots must be manifested and disposed of as non-hazardous solid waste in accordance with MiAmbiente regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The facility must obtain a fire-safety inspection certificate from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, a structural load and occupancy clearance certified by a licensed engineer and accepted by the local municipality, and a workplace health-and-safety acknowledgment filed with MITRADEL covering emergency exits, ventilation, electrical grounding, lighting, and fire suppression equipment for the green coffee warehouse.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance (Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas), accessible via the taxpayer portal 'Sede Electrónica' at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Panama Sociedad Anónima must be incorporated with the Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) through a licensed resident agent or local attorney. The company then must obtain an 'Aviso de Operación' (Business Operation Notice) and secure a 'Registro Único de Contribuyente' (RUC) by applying through the DGI Sede Electrónica. The procedure requires submission of the Public Registry certificate, bylaws (Escritura Pública), identification and residency of the legal representative or resident agent, local tax address, and projected turnover. Upon approval, the DGI issues the RUC certificate and registers the entity for ITBMS. A foreign entity without Panamanian incorporation is instead required to register a branch/sucursal or permanent establishment with the DGI and obtain a separate RUC before engaging in any Panama-source economic activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope (entity-level taxation limited to Panama-source income; a Sociedad Anónima is an opaque, limited-liability legal entity subject to Panamanian corporate income tax only on income sourced within Panama, including export transactions where title passes in Panama).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not maintain a U.S.-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election system. Available statutory elections include: (i) the small-taxpayer simplified regime (Régimen Simplificado de Pequeños Contribuyentes) for annual gross receipts up to B/.150,000, replacing standard ITBMS with a reduced progressive charge; (ii) application for a Multinational Headquarters (SEM) License or other preferential regimes (Panama Pacifico, Colón Free Zone) for eligible exporters and service providers; (iii) election to operate as a Panama branch (sucursal) of a foreign corporation rather than forming a local subsidiary; (iv) for holding structures, election under specific collective investment vehicle rules limited to the Panama Financial Code. No general check-the-box election is available for recharacterizing a Panama corporation for domestic tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) - Panama's VAT-style transaction tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general neutral turnover threshold; every enterprise with an Aviso de Operación that sells taxable goods or services in Panama must register for ITBMS. A simplified small-taxpayer regime applies to taxpayers with gross annual income not exceeding B/.150,000, subject to a charge of 2%–3% on domestic taxable sales (Law 18 of 2020).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing through the DGI 'e-Factura / SIFE' (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica) platform under DGI Resolution No. 201-1449 and subsequent amendments. Taxpayers must issue invoices using online real-time API, secure web portal, or system-to-system XML upload. Before issuance the DGI assigns a unique fiscal folio and a quick-response (QR) code; export invoices must transmit a zero-rated reason code and reference the supporting customs export declaration. Failure to obtain clearance will invalidate the invoice for purposes of crediting ITBMS and claiming export zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of specialty green coffee beans from Panama qualify for the 0% ITBMS rate when legal title passes to a foreign buyer and the goods physically leave Panamanian territory within six months of invoicing. The sale must be evidenced by an export contract, the DUA (Declaración Única de Exportación) validated by the National Customs Authority, and either a bill of lading or air waybill showing the foreign destination. Related offshore services (freight, insurance, international certification, and inspection) performed exclusively in favor of the foreign purchaser may also be zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: National Customs Authority (ANA) validated Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Declaración Única de Exportación)
Commercial invoice and detailed packing list matching the shipment
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Panama
Inward payment remittance certificate (SWIFT telegraphic transfer or documentary letter of credit confirmation) showing receipt of export proceeds by the Panamanian exporter
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI commonly audits export zero-rating claims, especially in agricultural value-chain transactions, within the statutory three-year prescription period (extendable to six years for fraudulent cases). If the exporter cannot substantiate the physical exit of goods or receipt of foreign currency within 180 days, the DGI retroactively recharacterizes the sale as domestic and assesses the 7% ITBMS plus a monthly late-payment recargo surcharge capped by law, default interest on the unpaid tax, and fines for non-compliant invoicing. In cases where falsified customs declarations or fabricated remittance evidence are found, the penalty increases to between 100% and 200% of the tax evaded, and criminal fiscal-fraud sanctions (including imprisonment under Panama's Fiscal Code and Law 18 of 2020) may be imposed. Exporters must retain the DUA, shipping documents, payment files, and contract records for at least six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) - the Superintendency of Banks of Panama - is the primary banking and AML/CFT regulator under Decreto Ley 9 de 1998 and Ley 23 de 2015; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent of the State. Panama has no traditional central bank and no foreign-exchange administration; it operates under full dollarization, with the U.S. Dollar as legal tender and the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) existing only as divisional coinage at fixed parity of 1 USD = 1 PAB.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account. Panama maintains IMF Article VIII status with no exchange controls, no central bank approval requirements, no waiting periods, and no quantitative restrictions on inbound equity, trade payments, loan servicing, or profit repatriation. Profit remittance is subject solely to the territorial dividend tax collection mechanism of the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI): a 5% withholding on dividends paid out of net taxable Panamanian-source profits (10% where profits were not subject to corporate tax), which must be declared and paid before the beneficiary wire is released. Once the DGI form is filed, the USD wire is unrestricted. Balboa coins have no commercial clearing application; all banking, clearing, and hedging flows are USD-denominated.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory repatriation deadline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no escrow requirement for green-coffee export receipts. Exporters may retain 100% of proceeds in USD in any SBP-licensed bank. The only administrative obligations are: (a) electronic export declaration (DUI/DEX) filed with the Dirección General de Aduanas for customs statistics; and (b) retention of bills of lading, phytosanitary certificates, commercial invoices, and SWIFT payment messages in the bank's AML file under Ley 23 de 2015 recordkeeping rules.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Current Account; Capital Escrow / Shareholder-Loan Sub-Account
Operational USD Current Account; Documentary Letter of Credit Facility

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BAC International Bank, Inc. (BAC Credomatic Panama)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational USD Current Account; Trade Finance Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Airwallex, Mercury, Payoneer) generally deprioritize or reject newly formed Panamanian S.A.s due to Panama's historically elevated FATF risk profile, enhanced correspondent-bank due diligence, and limited data-passing interoperability with Panama's residency-agent infrastructure. Under Panamanian law, any entity acting as a payment service provider or payment acquirer requires SBP authorization; an unlicensed non-bank EMI cannot lawfully hold Panamanian corporate funds as principal or intermediate cross-border payment flows. Feasibility is acceptable only as a nominal collection channel for small-ticket Western-European roaster payments routed onward to the Panama operating account within 24 hours, and never as the primary treasury or clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory for non-resident-owned S.A.s. At least one natural-person director or authorized signatory and each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) must complete an in-person KYC interview with bank compliance, either in Panama City or before a Panamanian consular official with notarization, supported by apostilled corporate documents (Hague Convention 1961), certified shareholder register, UBO declaration under Ley 23 de 2015 and Ley 254 de 2020, resident-agent good-standing letter, and valid passports. Fully remote digital account opening is generally not permitted under SBP due-diligence expectations; a minority of private banks accept a live videoconference interview in lieu of physical attendance, subject to enhanced due-diligence, relationship deposit, and U.S.-correspondent approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: registered bearer shares, nominee shareholders, or an incomplete beneficial-ownership filing for the S.A.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized UBO affidavit and beneficial-ownership registry receipt under Ley 23 de 2015 and Ley 254 de 2020; certified Libro de Accionistas (shareholder register) exhibited by the registered agent; sworn declaration that no bearer shares are outstanding; apostilled certificate of good standing and articles of incorporation; certified passport copies of all natural-person UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: First capital injection arriving from third-country personal accounts with an unexplained source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve-month bank statements of each subscribing shareholder; notarized source-of-wealth letter covering salary, dividend, or asset-disposal proceeds; shareholder resolution splitting the contribution between registered capital (USD 10,000) and paid-in surplus; escrow agreement executed pre-onboarding; bank reference letter from the originating institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-payment mismatch: wire beneficiary does not exactly match the green-coffee supplier on the commercial invoice or LC, or the origin country is on an OFAC/EU restricted list.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade-pack: signed coffee purchase contract (ICO-compliant terms), supplier commercial invoice, phytosanitary certificate, valid Certificate of Origin, clean on-board bill of lading with matching container numbers, prior-shipment MT103 records showing the same beneficiary, OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening report, and a signed compliance attestation naming the exact payee and vessel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Volumetric anomaly: monthly disbursement outflows exceed forecast by more than 100% without any LC, inventory, or financing documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Annual cash-flow budget and purchase-pipeline schedule; warehouse receipts and container-tracking summary; executed sale contracts with downstream roasters; copies of MT700/LC instruments covering the period; updated interim financial statements and stamped DGI tax filings demonstrating alignment with the declared Low_Risk_Standard profile.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) board/shareholder resolution approving the capital issuance and contribution; (2) MT103 wire from the subscribing shareholder's bank to the Panama S.A.'s USD operating account at Banco General or Banistmo with remittance narrative exactly stating 'Capital Contribution - Share Subscription' and the company RUC in the beneficiary information block; (3) full Travel Rule originator and beneficiary data embedded per Ley 23 de 2015; (4) 48-hour advance notification to the receiving bank with the complete documentation pack, including notarized minutes, certified shareholder register update, apostilled incorporation deed, and source-of-funds statements. No exchange-control declaration is required; the receiving bank may impose a compliance hold until the funds are reconciled against the contribution minutes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for specialty green-coffee settlements: (a) open-account payments via SWIFT MT103 in USD cleared through the Panamanian bank's U.S. correspondent (CHIPS/Fedwire) directly to the supplier's bank; (b) documentary Letters of Credit issued as MT700/MT720 under UCP600, typically 60-90 days tenor, with document sets comprising commercial invoice, full set of clean on-board bills of lading, phytosanitary certificate, ICA/SCA quality and weight certificate, and Certificate of Origin; (c) domestic USD disbursements within Panama clear through the ACH network (ACH Panama) and the clearing house administered by Banco Nacional de Panamá, while all high-value USD transfers including LC reimbursements settle via the U.S. correspondent leg, as Panama maintains no central-bank-operated RTGS system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (USD/EUR, USD/GBP, USD/COP) executed with an SBP-licensed bank under a short-form FX master agreement or ISDA/CSA; off-exchange and exempt from SMV public-offering registration.
Cross-Currency Swaps (USD/EUR and USD/GBP) for hedging trade-finance obligations, European warehouse financing, or phased supplier payments denominated in foreign currency.
FX Swaps and rolling spot contracts for converting EUR/GBP coffee-export collections into USD working capital.
European-style FX Options (calls and puts) on USD/EUR and USD/COP purchased from licensed banks to cap coffee-origin supplier cost volatility.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): not prohibited by Panamanian law, but no domestic deliverable PAB/USD market exists; permissible only with an offshore counterparty (London/New York) referencing a third-country base currency such as USD/EUR or USD/COP, with master agreement executed outside Panama.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax on Corporations — Impuesto Anual de Personas Jurídicas (base tier USD 150 for registered capital up to USD 10,000; USD 250 for USD 10,001–USD 50,000; maximum USD 1,500 for higher capital bands)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas — filed through the DGI TAT/e-Tax platform and collected by Banco Nacional de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 31 March for the immediately preceding calendar year; newly incorporated S.As are exempt from the annual tax for the year of incorporation and begin paying in the following March cycle; no extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge on the unpaid tax plus 1% monthly interest; two consecutive unpaid years result in the DGI notifying the Registro Público, which declares the corporation 'suspended/inactive'; continued non-payment thereafter risks administrative strike-off of the S.A. record

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return — Declaración Anual de Renta (Form 1219, taxable income limited to Panama-source revenues under territorial taxation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March following a 31 December fiscal year-end (standard S.A. calendar year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge (recargo) on tax due, interest of 1% per month, administrative fines for late/non-filing (up to USD 5,000 under Ley 134 de 2020), and DGI's right to assess income tax 'de oficio' from registered records

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation — Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final under Ley 254 de 2021 and Decreto Ejecutivo 5112 de 2022
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI — Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF) electronic registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March, coincident with the franchise-tax cycle; the declaration must reflect all shareholdings and transfers in force as of the filing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary fines from USD 500 to USD 5,000 per omission under the UBO enforcement rules; the DGI will not validate the annual franchise tax without a successfully filed UBO declaration, and the entity is denied good-standing certificates and blocked from Public Registry transactions until rectified

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements — Estados Financieros Auditados by a Panama-licensed certified public accountant (mandatory when annual gross income exceeds USD 250,000)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI — submitted as an attachment to Form 1219; copy retained by the shareholders in the corporate record book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March with the income tax return (no automatic extension for the audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Annual return treated as incomplete; DGI may assess taxes 'de oficio', apply accounting-obligation fines up to USD 5,000, and the registered agent may withhold continuing representation until the audited statements are delivered

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Resident Agent Annual Compliance Consent and Register Audit — Certificado de Agente Residente evidencing continuity of the legal domicile and verification of statutory registers/UBO records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Panamanian resident agent (abogado or regulated corporate services firm) with no direct Public Registry filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First calendar quarter of each year, contemporaneous with the franchise-tax payment and UBO declaration; agent's electronic consent is required for the DGI forms
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to satisfy the agent's compliance review forces the agent to resign; unresolved resignation causes Public Registry suspension of the corporate file, loss of good standing, and inoperability of bank/LC relationships

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Good Standing Certificate — Certificado de Persona Jurídica (not a periodic return; obtained after the March franchise-tax cycle for LC documentation, coffee-sales counterparties, and bank renewals)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, acting on proof of payment of the annual franchise tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Issued on request throughout the year, customarily refreshed within 5–10 business days after 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Refusal of issuance until all franchise-tax, UBO, and agent-compliance requirements are cleared; outstanding delinquency in the Public Registry file can interrupt documentary-letter-of-credit transactions and vessel-related financings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Entities with annual gross income exceeding USD 250,000 must file audited financial statements certified by a public accountant licensed in Panama (Código Fiscal Art. 715, as amended by Ley 134 de 2020); S.As below this threshold remain exempt but must keep books under IFRS and may be asked by the DGI to submit certified statements in specific audit cycles; voluntary audits are recommended for LC/banking support.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as issued by the IASB and adopted by the Colegio de Contadores Públicos Autorizados de Panamá; IFRS for SMEs is permissible for qualifying non-public entities without public accountability.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial-source taxation: margins from green coffee purchased abroad and containerized to foreign buyers are outside Panama-source income (Fiscal Code Art. 145) and effectively escape ISR; Multinational Headquarters (SEM) relief grants 0% on foreign-source coordination income and 5% on qualified domestic services; tax-loss carryforward of 5 years (Law 24 of 2019); no net-wealth tax and no CFC rules currently in force.
